$Comment: Icon intentionally omitted: StationService#blockItemIdAt already falls back to the anchor block's own BlockType id at engage time when Identity.Icon is absent/blank, and this jar's own default Sawmill block shares the same id (RPG_Station_Sawmill, filename = item id) - so the summary-HUD crest already shows the station's own block icon with zero duplicated id to drift, the same reasoning the pack's own Sawmill.json/Anvil.json use. Loot.Lootables is the unified LootRef group (asset.LootRef); Recipe here authors only FromCrafting, never Conversions. FromCrafting.Categories includes 'WoodPlanks', 'DecorativePlanks', and 'OrnatePlanks' - genuine native categories (every Wood_<Species>_{Planks,Decorative,Ornate}.json shares the same Wood_<Species>_Trunk ResourceTypeId input and the same 'Builders'/StructuralCrafting bench, only the recipe Category differs), so this is native-recipe composition, not invented content. The deriver surfaces 3 output categories per log species (33 total conversions); StationRecipeDeriver stamps each derived Conversion with its source category so the sneak+F picker can offer 'Planks'/'Decorative'/'Ornate' as the three choices for whatever log the player is holding - a single-log input, multiple valid outputs, exactly the picker's reason to exist. Recipe.Yield is the sawmill's yield edge over the plain Builders bench, and it is resolved fresh every cycle off the tool actually being held. Base 2 doubles the hand-craft yield: every derived recipe in all three categories authors native OutputQuantity 1 against a single-trunk Input, true across all 11 wood species (e.g. Wood_Hardwood_Planks / Wood_Hardwood_Decorative / Wood_Hardwood_Ornate), so 2 is exactly double with no per-category skew. Bonus is the tool ladder: its Values sum tool quality (the native ItemQuality.QualityValue - Junk 0, Common 1, Uncommon 2, Rare 3, Epic 4, Legendary 5) at weight 1.0 plus gather power at weight 2.0, and the single floor at 5.0 adds one more plank. Both terms are load-bearing rather than one being decoration: hatchet Woods power SATURATES at 0.5 from the mid ladder up, so power alone cannot separate the top tiers, while quality alone would ignore how effective the tool is. The result across the vanilla hatchets is Epic (Mithril, Onyxium) = 4 + 1.0 = 5.0 -> 3 planks, Rare (Cobalt, Thorium, Adamantite) = 3 + 1.0 = 4.0 -> 2, Uncommon Iron = 2 + 0.6 -> 2, Common (Wood, Crude, Copper) ~1.4 -> 2. Every number here is a tunable leaf: reweight the two Values to change what the curve rewards, move the floor Min to change which tier earns the extra plank, or append another floor with a larger Add for a higher tier (floors are not cumulative - the highest one reached wins). An added Scale/Min/Max would compose on top. A station deriving categories whose native recipes are NOT 1:1 should author Scale instead of Base, since the native quantity is not readable at the derivation seam. A plain-F press with no picker selection defaults to the first authored FromCrafting.Categories entry - so the array order below (WoodPlanks first) is the default priority (the deriver's alphabetical output-id sort would otherwise make Decorative the first runnable). Reorder Categories to change the plain-F default; sneak+F still offers all three. This is resolved engine-side at the effective-category point (StationService#effectiveCategory), not the deriver sort, so the balance-neutral claim above stays true. The Puppet group, Custody.Display, and Work.CycleMs 4805 below are this jar's own shipped standalone defaults, tuned in-game so the standalone sawmill looks right with no pack installed: Puppet.Offset.Z 1.0 and Yaw 0.0 position the working puppet at the bench; Custody.Display.Offset.Y -0.1 embeds the placed log slightly into the bench top; Work.CycleMs 4805 is the tuned cadence. ExtensionAsset carries real Puppet/Custody keys with per-leaf overlay semantics, so a pack re-skinning this station authors only the leaves it re-tunes and inherits the rest of these defaults - see asset/ExtensionAsset.java rule 5 and station/ExtensionCatalog.java's overlayPuppet/overlayCustody. Work declares no PerCycleContributions: this jar's content is progression-free by design, and a pack layers its own on through an ExtensionAsset. Tool.PowerScale is deliberately KEPT even with nothing to scale - the tool ladder is pre-wired and tuned, so a pack that appends contributions inherits a working power curve for free rather than re-deriving one.
